title: Pickpockets working downtown near the depots
summary: They worked downtown near the stations, not uptown clubs, and came to the club to spend money and give her lots of tips.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I see. Well, what about in the clubs? They wouldn't pick pockets in the clubs?

Out. They'd all go downtown, downtown. They wouldn't pick pockets uptown. They all go downtown where most of the businessmen or travelling people -- they hung out more or less around the stations. We called it the depots, up north, but dee-pots, down south. And they would rob those people.
Never harm them or anything, but just talk to them and get their money.

Where the money -- yes, where the money was. That's what they'd do. And then they'd all come in there and sit around and buy each other drinks and open wine and all that kind of stuff, and give me all kinds of money. Just all kinds of money. So then, after we left Hugh Hoskins, then's when we went up to the -- to -- let me see, did I work at the De Luxe first, or -- I went to the Panama.
